title: The Black Death Arrives
objective: After this level you can explain how the Black Death reached Europe in 1347.
summary: The Black Death began in Central Asia, struck the Mongol siege of Caffa in 1346, and reached Messina on ships in October 1347. By 1350 it had crossed Europe, killing an estimated 30-50% of its people.

cards.headline: October 1347: ships reach Sicily carrying a passenger nobody can see.
cards.body: Within a few years it had crossed the whole continent. Where did the Black Death come from, and how many people did it kill?

cards.headline: It began far to the east
cards.body: The trail starts in Central Asia. Near Lake Issyk-Kul, in today’s Kyrgyzstan, graves with tombstones dated 1338 and 1339 held plague DNA, pointing there as the source. By 1346 it had reached Crimea, where a Mongol army besieging the Italian trading port of Caffa began to die of it. One chronicler claimed the besiegers catapulted corpses over the walls, though he probably wasn’t there to see it. Genoese ships then carried the plague west.

events.label: Plague deaths near Lake Issyk-Kul, Central Asia
Plague strikes the siege of Caffa, in Crimea
Ships bring it to Messina, in Sicily

cards.headline: How many died?
cards.body: The numbers are estimates, and historians work them out differently. Most put the dead at about 30% to 50% of Europe’s population between 1347 and 1351. The historian Ole Benedictow calculated a higher figure: about 60%. In England, around a third of the people were dead by 1349. Picture a class photo. On the lower estimates, nearly a third of the faces are gone; on the higher ones, more than half.
cards.callout: Most estimates: about 30% to 50% of Europe

options.label: The figures are estimates, and historians calculate them differently
Records show exactly half died in every town
options.rationale: There are no exact counts; estimates vary.

The plague killed only children
options.rationale: It killed people of every age.
